The 1-month confidence interval (234.95 to 261.31) grows substantially wider because long-term forecasts inherently involve more unknowns, such as compounding small uncertainties over time, potential shifts in underlying conditions, or more extreme market events.

Certain risks or events could nudge or even push outcomes outside the stated intervals, particularly at the longer time horizons. Natural disasters or abrupt shifts in global markets could also lead to increased volatility and outcomes significantly outside the predicted range. Additionally, any model assumptions that have been employed might fail to capture unusual or rare events, which could mean the intervals do not fully encompass the tail risks for extremely unlikely but impactful scenarios.
